# Frustum and Visibility Culling

Also called: Frustum Culling, Visibility Culling, Frustum-Occlusion Culling

## Overview
Frustum and Visibility Culling optimizes volume rendering by discarding geometric primitives that lie outside the camera's viewing volume, thereby reducing the computational load on empty or background regions. It distinguishes itself from sibling methods by operating at the scene or subtree level to filter entire hierarchies or splat batches before traversal or rasterization, rather than performing per-ray intersection tests within the volume data.

## Shared principles
All methods in this family share the core mechanism of hierarchical descent and ascent. The traversal begins at the root of the octree and determines which of the eight children (octants) the ray intersects. This is typically done by comparing the ray's position relative to the center of the current node's bounding box [S1][S2, unofficial][S6, S8, unofficial].

1.  **Child Selection:** For a node with center $\mathbf{c}$ and half-extent $s$, the ray position $\mathbf{p}$ determines the child index $k \in \{0, \dots, 7\}$:
    $$
    k = 4 \cdot \mathbb{I}(p_x \ge c_x) + 2 \cdot \mathbb{I}(p_y \ge c_y) + 1 \cdot \mathbb{I}(p_z \ge c_z)
    $$
    where $\mathbb{I}(\cdot)$ is the indicator function [S1][S2, unofficial][S6, S8, unofficial].

2.  **[Empty Space Skipping](#1002-empty-space-skipping.md):** If the selected child is marked as empty (or uniform), the traversal skips the subtree. This is achieved by advancing the ray parameter $t$ to the exit of the current node or using neighbor pointers to jump to the next potentially occupied node [S1, S6, S8, unofficial][G].

3.  **Leaf Handling:** Upon reaching a leaf node, the method typically switches to a fixed-step traversal (like DDA) within the leaf's voxel grid to sample the volume data [S1, S6, S8, unofficial][G].

4.  **Backtracking:** Because octrees are sparse and irregular, traversal often requires backtracking to the parent node when a ray exits a subtree or encounters an empty branch. This is implemented using an explicit stack (on GPU) or recursion (on [CPU](#10688-naive-sdf-generation-cpu.md)) [S4, S6, S8, unofficial].

## Subtopics

### [Bounding-Sphere Tree Traversal with Frame-Rate Control](7227-bounding-sphere-tree-traversal-with-frame-rate-control.md)
This method renders hierarchical [tree structures](#4139-tree-based-structures-octree-pointer-tree-sparse-voxel-dag.md) (specifically Shell and Solid trees) using point-based [splatting](#23-splatting.md) primitives, solving the problem of maintaining real-time frame rates for large volumetric datasets by dynamically adjusting rendering fidelity [7227-bounding-sphere-tree-traversal-with-frame-rate-control.md]. It distinguishes itself from standard [octree traversal](#1587-octree-traversal.md) by replacing fixed-resolution [voxel stepping](#832-amanatides-woo-voxel-traversal.md) with adaptive bounding-sphere culling and frame-rate feedback loops that control the minimum splat size in screen space [7227-bounding-sphere-tree-traversal-with-frame-rate-control.md].

### [Frustum Culling Integration](8798-frustum-culling-integration.md)
[Frustum Culling Integration](#8798-frustum-culling-integration.md) is a visibility [optimization technique](#7922-optimization-technique.md) applied during the progressive loading of volumetric splats (specifically 3D [Gaussian Splatting](#946-gaussian-splatting.md)) to prioritize data transmission and rendering of elements within the user's current view [8798-frustum-culling-integration.md]. It operates by filtering out splats that lie outside the viewing frustum, thereby reducing the computational load on background elements [8798-frustum-culling-integration.md]. Unlike the base octree-only approach, which provides a static scene representation without user-specific knowledge, this method leverages the user's initial pose to improve performance when such information is available [8798-frustum-culling-integration.md].

### [Frustum-Occlusion Culling for Octree Traversal](12324-frustum-occlusion-culling-for-octree-traversal.md)
This method identifies a set of visible voxels by traversing an octree hierarchy and comparing each node against the camera's view frustum [12324-frustum-occlusion-culling-for-octree-traversal.md]. It serves as a [visibility culling](#6226-visibility-culling.md) and Level-of-Detail (LOD) selection mechanism for [voxel rasterization](#3204-voxel-rasterization.md), ensuring that only octants intersecting the frustum and large enough to project onto at least one pixel are processed [12324-frustum-occlusion-culling-for-octree-traversal.md]. It differs from standard ray-marching octree traversal by operating in screen-space to cull entire subtrees based on projected area, rather than per-ray intersection tests [12324-frustum-occlusion-culling-for-octree-traversal.md].
